literal_meaning: খাওয়া এবং মুক্তি/পরিশোধ (আয় থেকে ঋণ মিটানোর অর্থে)
figurative_meaning_en: Repaying a loan from the income derived from the land
example_sentences_in_bangla: গ্রামের অনেক কৃষক খাই-খালাসির শর্তে জমি চাষ করে ঋণ শোধ করে।
আমাদের পরিবার খাই-খালাসি করে বছরের ফসল থেকে সব ঋণ পরিশোধ করেছে।
example_sentences_in_english: Many farmers in the village cultivate land on khai-khalasi terms to repay their loans.
Our family has cleared all debts by sharecropping the harvest under khai-khalasi arrangement.
history: This idiom originates from the traditional Bengali agrarian system, particularly during the British colonial period, where 'khas' land (government-owned) was leased to tenants who repaid rent or loans directly from crop yields without fixed cash payments.
note: Refers to a specific form of tenancy in Bengal's rural history, emphasizing subsistence farming tied to debt clearance.
